column1: The Foreign Country To keep the analysis simple, it was assumed that the foreign country is large relative to the home country. This is taken to mean that it is unnecessary to distinguish between consumer price inflation and domestic inflation in the foreign country and that domestic output and consumption are equal. Trade does take place, however, and so goods produced in the home country are sold to domestic residents and to foreigners.
